text:
marina: kicking off bring-up for new region 'sea5' (ap-northeast-2) — target: GPU pool + vpc + TF/Pulumi wiring. planning window 48h. need volunteers for state bridge and ci/cd pipelines :wave:
chris: i'll own pulumi modules and cluster manifests. have the custom kernel/kv-cache changes ready, just need state handoff plan.
devon: i'll take terraform side (network, peering, quotas). quick q — are we using the existing statebucket or creating a regional bucket?
marina: prefer regional bucket for latency + compliance. create bucket with lifecycle 90d and encryption. we'll set up state-bridge to S3 backend in main account.
chris: ok. plan: create pulumi stacks: sea5-infra, sea5-cluster. pulumi backend = regional bucket. need a short maintenance window to lock tfstate during import.
alex: quick note on quotas — provider flagged GPU quota soft-limit in the region. I opened ticket with cloud: case# 984312. expect approval ~6-8hrs. we should still stage networking and bootstrap without instances.
sanjay: also double-check CIDR overlap with customer VPC peering maps. last time we hit overlap and had to re-IP the subnet which delayed rollout.
marina: good catch. devon, can you run the overlap check script? 
devon: running now: `./scripts/check-cidr-overlap --region ap-northeast-2`. output: one conflict with corp-analytics (10.40.0.0/16 vs planned 10.40.0.0/18). recommend changing cluster pod subnet to 10.41.0.0/16.
chris: that's fine. I'll update pulumi config to podCidr=10.41.0.0/16 and regen manifests. will push a draft PR.
marina: for state handoff: plan is 1) create regional s3 bucket + KMS key 2) export current tf state for related infra resources (vpc, routes) 3) import into pulumi stack using `pulumi import` for critical resources 4) lock original state and annotate handoff ticket.
chris: for imports, mapping note: we must import loadbalancer IDs and LB target groups before cluster creation to avoid controller churn. snippet I'll use:
```
# import example
pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc sea5-vpc vpc-0a1b2c3d
pulumi import aws:lb/targetGroup:TargetGroup sea5-tg arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/sea5-tg/abcd
```

alex: CI/CD wiring — we need a new pipeline in ci/infrastructure with two gated steps: `plan` + manual approve -> `apply`. Also add a validation step to run `kubeconform` against manifests.
sanjay: +1 for kubeconform. also add a cheap smoke test that creates a single inference pod on a small GPU instance (g4dn.xlarge) to verify driver + kernel modules.
marina: agree. devon — please add the smoke job to the terraform/cicd job matrix and tag it to run only during region bring-up.
devon: done, draft CI config in `ci/sea5-pipeline.yml`. includes plan/apply, wait-for-quota, smoke-check.
chris: one more cost note — we should start with a minimal GPU pool size (1-2 nodes) and auto-scale based on queued jobs. recommend using spot for initial canary but with fallback to on-demand. will add autoscaler config and spot/ondemand fallback policy to pulumi cluster stack.
marina: good. timeline: prep + infra (6-8h) -> import + cluster bootstrap (6-10h) -> smoke + validation (2-4h) -> handoff + docs (2h). total ~24h workable.
deploy-bot: deployment queued: `ci/sea5-pipeline` plan started by chris at 1768506000.
chris: pushing PRs now: pulumi: `github.com/redwood/pulumi/compare/sea5-boot`, tf: `github.com/redwood/terraform/compare/sea5-network`. tagging @devops-review for final check.
marina: thanks — i'll coordinate handoff with solutions and sales for region availability ETA. ping here with blockers. :thumbsup:
